transcript: What if the greatest obstacle between you and the love of your life was walking down a flight of stairs? But what should be a simple trip becomes its own odyssey. That's the premise of I'm almost there, currently playing at BAM. I actually don't want to spoil too much of this show because this is a musical that is best experienced for yourself. But I saw it for the first time two years ago at the Edinburgh Fringe and I haven't stopped thinking about so much so that I saw it again when it came to New York for the first time at the Audible Theater. And now two years later, it's at BAM, which is kind of the perfect venue for this quirky little show. What I love the most about it is how deeply New York it feel. It's hilarious and romantic and filled with weird neighbours. It's a story of self discovery, of overcoming your deepest fears and ultimately of realising you are worthy of love. I also got invited to attend a special event for the show, which was really exciting. Todd Almond, who wrote and stars in the show, played a couple of the songs and there was a talk back with Todd and director David Cromer, hosted by Mary Louise Parker, who has no connection to the show other than the fact that she's obsessed with it and want to talk about it and kept calling Tad Hammond a genius. And honestly, I relate to That. Anyway, here are a few clips from I'm almost there. You're never gonna believe this. And he walks over to me and he goes, I was just leaving to get a coffee. You wanna join me? And I go, yeah. And we just walk away. And the neighbor says to me, I have friends, but I think I'm the kind of. I keep on trying, but I'm only almost. You only have one more week to catch. I'm almost there at Bam! If you're looking for something original, moving, and unlike anything else playing in New York right now, this is your show.
